body: Trauma Center: Under the Knife 2 is Vanguard and Atlus' Nintendo DS surgical thriller continuing the story of Derek Stiles three years after the first game. The return of the GUILT disease draws him back into dangerous medical work, alongside the personal uncertainty and institutional pressures surrounding his profession. Story scenes lead into operations performed with the stylus, retaining the original handheld arrangement. The sequel returns to the same surgeon and working surface, allowing the player's familiarity with his instruments to meet a new sequence of patients and emergencies.

The available instruments include a scalpel, laser, ultrasound and defibrillator, each selected from icons around the touchscreen. Treating a patient may require dealing with surface wounds and internal injuries while watching the time limit and vital signs. Antibiotic gel and other support tools help maintain the condition needed to complete the procedure. Different difficulty settings provide another way into the demanding sequences. The work still depends on recognising which problem should be treated next, then carrying out the appropriate movement without allowing another urgent condition to become unmanageable.

GUILT strains turn selected procedures into confrontations with an artificial threat inside the patient. Derek's Healing Touch remains available when the situation calls for his exceptional ability, connecting a supernatural story element with the timing of the player's actions. Portraits and conversations give the medical team space between those emergencies. Under the Knife 2 builds on an already recognisable set of tools, using the continuing story to give another operation a different context and another reason to care about completing the procedure before the patient's condition becomes critical.
